idea-plugin.name: Giuan Tomcat
idea-plugin.description:
Run Tomcat 9 directly from IntelliJ IDEA

"Giuan Tomcat" adds a Giuan Tomcat run configuration that starts an Apache Tomcat 9 instance without requiring the bundled Tomcat integration or any external plugin: the plugin auto-generates the CATALINA_BASE (conf, logs, work, temp, webapps), writes server.xml and the per-application context.xml, and launches Bootstrap with full native IntelliJ debug support (breakpoints, variables, stack traces).

  • No build/deploy step — the selected modules' target/classes and dependency jars are mounted directly on /WEB-INF/classes and /WEB-INF/lib.
  • Startup scan skip — two independent switches to disable Tomcat's startup scanning and speed up boot on large applications:
    • Skip jar scan (per module): for each module ticked in the Selected list, the plugin writes a <JarScanner>/<JarScanFilter> block in the generated context.xml. For the context it sets reloadable="false" and containerSciFilter (keeps only the websocket SCI), disables scanClassPath, scanBootstrapClassPath, scanAllDirectories and scanAllFiles, and lists the names of the dependency jars of the flagged modules in pluggabilitySkip and tldSkip. What is skipped: Tomcat's scan of the ServletContainerInitializer (SCI)/annotations (pluggability) and of the JSP Tag Library descriptors (TLD/taglib) of exactly those jars. The jars of non-flagged modules are still scanned and the jars remain mounted and usable.
    • Skip annotation scan (global): on run the plugin edits the WEB-INF/web.xml of the web content, adding metadata-complete="true" to the <web-app> element and an empty <absolute-ordering/>. What is skipped: Servlet 3.0 annotation scanning (@WebServlet/@WebFilter/...) and the discovery and processing of web-fragments and ServletContainerInitializer registered in the application jars. The additions are tracked with a marker comment so that disabling the option on a later run removes exactly what the plugin added; any pre-existing metadata-complete/<absolute-ordering> are left untouched. Changes are applied idempotently.
  • Simple configuration — choose CATALINA_HOME, CATALINA_BASE, web content (docBase), context path and HTTP/shutdown ports from a single dialog.
  • Optional HotSwap mode (Java 8 + DCEVM + hotswap-agent) — enable unlimited runtime class redefinition (add/remove fields and methods without restarting). DCEVM is always forced when HotSwap is active, in Run and Debug alike; in Debug the IDE debugger performs the reload (JDWP), in Run the agent watches target/classes automatically (autoHotswap).
  • Generated instance reuse — the same CATALINA_BASE can be shared between run configurations and started again after it is stopped.

HotSwap prerequisites (see the guide in the plugin repository): a JDK 8 (8u181) patched with DCEVM (-XXaltjvm=dcevm) and a hotswap-agent.jar downloaded from the HotswapAgent releases. Web applications must be compiled with Java 8 bytecode.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 2.3.0 Skip scan: per-module jar-scan skip now also sets reloadable="false", containerSciFilter and disables classpath/bootstrap/all-directory/all-file scanning in context.xml; the global annotation-scan skip also writes <absolute-ordering/> into WEB-INF/web.xml.
  • 2.2.1 Replace deprecated LibraryOrSdkOrderEntry.getFiles() with getRootFiles().
  • 2.2.0 HotSwap for Java 8 only: a JDK with DCEVM already installed is assumed. Agent configured per the hotswapagent.org guide (-XXaltjvm=dcevm -javaagent:hotswap-agent.jar). Removed the Java version selection and the automatic JDK/DCEVM download.
  • 2.1.0 Add optional HotSwap mode (DCEVM + hotswap-agent).
  • 2.0.0 Convert to Gradle-based plugin.
  • 1.0.0 Release 2018.3 and earlier.
